location: cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Producers + Fields (null fields) vs State, freshness > Fresh vs Plan step 3 blocked-infra (test) and rerun reason 'not-run'
issue: Records that ps-run-layer writes itself (no-slots, not-run, crash, stopped, browser-unavailable, keeper-start) have no image_tag. image_tag comes only from the child ('The child emits per version ... image_tag'), and 'null for fields no engine produced' applies. Fresh requires image_tag == resolved tag, so these records are never fresh. That contradicts two things: (a) the blocked-infra rule and its test ('two no-slots records in one session on one fingerprint give blocked-infra'), which need both records to be fresh; (b) the plan reason 'not-run', which is only reachable 'by the newest fresh record', so a newest not-run record reads as 'stale-tag'. ps-run-layer cannot fill the tag either: Config keys says it reads from --config 'only the E2E keys below, the configured set and psm_flashlight_startup_timeout', which leaves out psm_flashlight_tag_map.
implementation_impact: The mandated blocked-infra test cannot pass as written, a repeated no-slots/crash loop never ends, and the not-run reason never surfaces. The warm pre-iteration check ('its image tag equals the resolved tag') also needs a tag that ps-run-layer is not allowed to resolve.
suggestion: Make ps-run-layer resolve the tag itself (from psm_flashlight_tag_map in --config plus any --tag-map/--extra-tag-map in the passthrough, via fl.resolve_tag) and stamp image_tag on every record it writes. Alternatively, define freshness for engine-less records as fingerprint-only.

location: cell-contract.md > Config keys > psm_e2e_slots (wait-slots bullet) vs Runner > Fail-fast ('ps-run-layer queues cells under the cap') vs SPEC CAP-3 success
issue: A cell that cannot get a slot waits in wait-slots 'for at most the startup timeout' (default 180 s), then gets no-slots. Nothing separates waiting on foreign load from queueing behind this run's own in-flight cells. A cold version run takes many minutes, so with a cap below the run's demand (e.g. psm_e2e_slots=2 in tier 1 with three versions, or the CAP-3 test with --slots 1 and three versions), every queued cell times out to no-slots instead of waiting its turn. In the CAP-3 scenario the queued cells would be recorded as no-slots long before the first cell's exit 3 could make them not-run.
implementation_impact: The implementer has to guess whether the startup-timeout bound applies to intra-run queueing. Implemented literally, any cap smaller than a tier's demand turns into inconclusive no-slots, and after two of those, blocked-infra. That defeats the 'queue under the cap' design and makes the CAP-3 live behaviour contradict its test.
suggestion: State that the timeout covers only time during which the run has nothing of its own in flight, or that it restarts whenever one of this run's own cells frees a slot. Cells blocked only by their own siblings wait without a bound. Add a test with slots < demand that expects no no-slots records.

location: cell-contract.md > Runner > Fail-fast + Config keys > psm_e2e_slots (slot_claims: 'a claim counts until a running container carries its psm.run or its process exits')
issue: The child tears down its container (in finally) before it exits with code 3. Once the container is gone the psm.slots label disappears, and the claim no longer counts because the container already ran, so the slot frees before ps-run-layer sees exit 3. A cell waiting in wait-slots (the CAP-3 test: --slots 1, three versions) can be admitted and start bring-up in that window, which breaks 'the progress log shows no bring-up for them'.
implementation_impact: CAP-3 becomes racy: the success test is flaky, and in production one extra cell may boot after a conclusive failure.
suggestion: Keep a child's claim counted until ps-run-layer has reaped the child's exit code, so admission is re-evaluated only after the fail-fast decision. Alternatively, have the version process signal 'fail' to ps-run-layer (e.g. a result file written before teardown) and check it under slots.lock before admitting.

location: cell-contract.md > Scenario prerequisites ('bankwire checkout-with-bank.json ... would declare') vs SPEC Non-goals ('Writing new E2E scenarios for any module') vs Success signal / live identical-findings test
issue: Whether bankwire's checkout-with-bank.json actually gets the 'requires' field is left as a conditional example. The live tests depend on it. The warm iteration resets the DB to a pre-install baseline, and the failed-only selection, and the rerun-seq on a post-warmup-bo dump, run only the failed scenario plus its 'requires'. Without the field, checkout-with-bank runs without its BO setup scenarios and fails or diverges for reasons unrelated to the injected expect_text fault. The identical-findings test then compares sets that differ by setup state, and the success-signal iteration after the revert patch does not pass.
implementation_impact: I would have to guess whether editing the bankwire fixture spec is in scope. If it is not, the CAP-4, CAP-5 and CAP-7 live tests are non-deterministic or fail.
suggestion: Make it an explicit deliverable: add 'requires' to modules/bankwire/tests/e2e/checkout-with-bank.json (or to the temp copy inside the live-test setup). Note that this is a fixture edit, not a new scenario.

location: tier-matrix.md > Tier 1 'Starts when' + Rules (Phase 1 bullet) / cell-contract.md > Plan > Phase 1 / SPEC Constraints (headless)
issue: 'Clean on Layers 1, 2, and 5' is defined only as phase1_reuse true ('no layer other than e2e and adversarial reruns'). That is freshness, not passing. The tier matrix reads it as passing ('every version clean'). Also, headless psm-validate never patches source. If 'clean' means passing, a headless run whose hosting version has a blocking Layer 2 error never reaches the E2E step, and its Phase 1 loop has no defined termination. If 'clean' means fresh, a module with a failing Layer 2 still burns E2E boots.
implementation_impact: The loop exit condition and the moment tier 0 is allowed to run would be guessed. Headless behaviour for a module that fails Layer 1/2/5 is undefined: possibly an infinite loop, or E2E skipped silently.
suggestion: Define 'clean' explicitly (I assume fresh, i.e. phase1_reuse) in tier-matrix and Plan > Phase 1. For headless, state that each Phase 1 loop runs once, and whether E2E runs when Layers 1/2/5 have blocking findings.

location: cell-contract.md > Plan > Phase 2 entry + bullet 'A run that prints e2e_status: skipped ... ends the E2E loop'
issue: The Phase 2 entry check requires a plan call showing 'e2e_step gate, done, or a step that ends the E2E loop'. e2e_status: skipped (Playwright/Docker absent) and psm_e2e_enabled false come from run output or orchestrator config, not from an e2e_step. After a skipped run, the plan still derives 'focus' (no record was written), so a literal Phase 2 entry check fails and 'the hosting loop for a tier-0 step run again', which repeats a step the text says must not be repeated.
implementation_impact: Read literally, the orchestrator procedure loops forever on machines without Playwright, or with E2E disabled.
suggestion: Add an orchestrator-side 'E2E loop ended' state (skipped / disabled / --require without e2e) that the Phase 2 entry check treats like a terminal step. Alternatively, have the plan accept an --e2e-disabled flag and emit e2e_step 'skipped'.

location: cell-contract.md > Plan > Phase 1 (phase1_reuse) / Phase 2 entry
issue: Without Docker, ps-run-layer never persists per-version flashlight/scenario files (skipped payloads are not written, ps-run-layer.py main). The plan therefore reports those layers as rerun forever, phase1_reuse never becomes true, and neither the hosting loop nor the Phase 2 entry check can ever pass. Today all_reuse was read by judgment. The new contract makes phase1_reuse a mechanical gate with no exit for 'layer unavailable on this host'.
implementation_impact: On a Docker-less host the mechanical procedure never reaches Phase 2 or the aggregate.
suggestion: Define phase1_reuse to ignore layers whose last run reported skipped (unavailable), or specify an orchestrator rule that ends Phase 1 when a Docker layer reports skipped.

location: cell-contract.md > Headless (return JSON: 'a version none of whose configured cells has a record carrying this call's --session ... gets reason not reached: stopped at <step>')
issue: No script computes this. The aggregate does not take --session, and the plan's outputs do not report which versions have records from the current session. The headless orchestrator (a prompt) would have to read the .jsonl histories by hand, which goes against SKILL.md's 'read verdicts as-is, do not reassemble' rule.
implementation_impact: I would have to guess where this logic goes: plan, aggregate or prose. If it goes in prose it is non-deterministic.
suggestion: Give ps-aggregate.py an optional --session and have it emit versions[ver].reached (or the 'not reached' reason) itself. Headless then copies it.

location: cell-contract.md > Aggregate (first bullet: '--config ... gains the plan's --tag-map/--extra-tag-map')
issue: The aggregate is said to read only the configured set from --config. It is not stated whether it also applies psm_flashlight_tag_map from that config (the plan does, via apply_config_file). If it does not, an operator with a custom tag map who passes only --config gets every record judged stale-tag in the aggregate while the plan calls them fresh.
implementation_impact: Plan and aggregate may disagree on freshness, which drops ready falsely.
suggestion: State that the aggregate resolves tags exactly as the plan does (apply psm_flashlight_tag_map from --config, explicit --tag-map wins), and add a test where config carries a non-default tag map.

location: cell-contract.md > Config keys (preamble: ps-run-layer reads only E2E keys...; psm_e2e_slots 'Maps to ps-run-layer.py --slots (CONFIG_KEY_TO_DEST in ps-flashlight-run.py)')
issue: CONFIG_KEY_TO_DEST is consumed by fl.apply_config_file, which also maps psm_target_versions -> versions and psm_flashlight_* keys. ps-run-layer is forbidden to map psm_target_versions -> --versions, so it cannot use apply_config_file with that table. Adding psm_e2e_slots to the shared table only affects children, which have no 'slots' dest. Where the --slots mapping actually lives is contradictory.
implementation_impact: Guesswork on how ps-run-layer loads config. Reusing apply_config_file as-is would silently fill --versions from config, which the contract forbids.
suggestion: Specify a separate ps-run-layer-only key map (psm_e2e_slots, psm_e2e_warm_ttl, psm_e2e_canary, psm_flashlight_startup_timeout, psm_flashlight_tag_map if the first finding is adopted), or an apply_config_file parameter that restricts the keys applied.

location: cell-contract.md > State, freshness, gate-grade > Fresh ('... psm_reports_dir and the run's screenshot directory when they lie inside it')
issue: Plan, runner and aggregate must share one fingerprint function, but only the runner knows the screenshot directory (--screenshot-dir arrives in ps-run-layer's passthrough). The plan and aggregate never receive it. If the screenshot dir lies inside the module dir and outside psm_reports_dir, the runner's fingerprint excludes it and the plan's includes it, so every record looks stale-source.
implementation_impact: Freshness can differ between producer and readers, which leads to endless reruns.
suggestion: Drop the screenshot-dir exclusion and require that the screenshot dir lie outside the module or inside psm_reports_dir (exit 2 otherwise). Alternatively, give plan and aggregate the same --screenshot-dir.

location: tier-matrix.md > Rules (Phase/Layer 3 bullet: 'A loop-back to tier 0 re-enters Phase 1, and Layer 3 output from before the new patch is stale and is spawned again')
issue: Layer 3 subagents are spawned at the start of Phase 2, concurrently with tier 1. If tier 1 fails and the loop goes back, those subagents may still be running. Nothing says to discard their results. If the orchestrator merges them after the fix patch, adversarial.json gets an mtime newer than the source, and the plan's mtime-based freshness treats a review of pre-patch code as fresh.
implementation_impact: Stale Layer 3 findings, or a stale 'clean' review, can gate the release.
suggestion: On loop-back, discard (do not merge) in-flight Layer 3 results, or merge them only when no patch has landed since spawn, e.g. by recording the source fingerprint at spawn time.

location: tier-matrix.md > Rules > Visual review (<module>-visual-pending.json)
issue: Pending visual defects are not tied to a fingerprint or run. A defect seen on the cold canary run in Phase 1 waits in visual-pending.json across a later loop-back patch that may have fixed it, and is then merged into adversarial.json in Phase 2 as a blocking finding against code that no longer has it. It is also unspecified what happens to pending entries when the session ends without reaching Phase 2.
implementation_impact: Stale blocking findings can drop ready, and leftover pending files from earlier sessions get merged into a new session.
suggestion: Record source_fingerprint (and session) with each pending entry. At merge time, drop entries whose fingerprint is not current or whose session differs, and log what was dropped.

location: cell-contract.md > Warm container > Owner (session.json fields)
issue: session.json lists 'orchestrator mode, container, DB and network names, compose project, published port...', but not the compose file path. fl._exec in compose mode needs session['compose_file'] ('docker compose -f <file> -p <project> exec'), and the keeper's tmpdir holding it is private. The iteration process cannot run reset, install or wait in compose mode with the listed fields.
implementation_impact: I would have to guess between adding the field and switching iterations to 'docker exec <ps_container>' in both modes.
suggestion: Add compose_file (and tmpdir) to session.json, or state that iterations always use plain 'docker exec' on the recorded PS container name.

location: cell-contract.md > Config keys > psm_e2e_warm_ttl ('the keeper validates it before it detaches (exit 2)') vs Warm container > Chain ('ps-run-layer ... starts one detached'; 'a keeper that exits first gives the cell an inconclusive record, reason keeper-start')
issue: It is unclear who detaches (ps-run-layer via start_new_session, or the keeper by forking itself), and whether a keeper exit 2 is an input error (no record, ps-run-layer exits 2) or a keeper-start inconclusive record. If the keeper daemonizes by forking after bring-up, the container's psm.owner-pid label points at a dead PID, and --cleanup-orphans would remove a live keeper's container.
implementation_impact: This affects keeper ownership safety and the exit-code and record semantics.
suggestion: State that ps-run-layer validates psm_e2e_warm_ttl at config load (exit 2, no keeper started) and launches the keeper as a new session without the keeper forking. If the keeper must fork, it has to do so before bring-up so the labels carry the final PID.

location: cell-contract.md > Warm container > Owner ('The On Activation report lists live keepers of other owner tokens for the module with their --stop-job command')
issue: No script or flag produces this list. --list-jobs shows registry entries without owner tokens, and keepers' session.json files live in <tmp>/psm-warm/, which nothing enumerates. The SKILL.md On Activation update is also missing from 'Docs to update' (only 'On Activation step 2 scope' is listed), and so is minting the session token there.
implementation_impact: The orchestrator would have to hand-parse tmp files, or the requirement gets dropped.
suggestion: Add a flag (e.g. ps-flashlight-run.py --list-warm --module <path>) that prints keepers with owner token, warm-id, age and stop command. Add 'On Activation: mint --new-session, list foreign keepers' to Docs to update.

location: cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Fields (boot_id) + Phase timings (warm iteration boot '<keeper boot_id>#<iteration RUN_ID>'; 'The iteration that started the keeper embeds the keeper's boot_phases in its record')
issue: A warm record's boot_id is either the keeper's RUN_ID ('RUN_ID of the process that ran bring-up') or the composite '<keeper boot_id>#<RUN_ID>'. The first iteration's record must carry two boots (the keeper's bring-up and the iteration's reset/install), but boot_phases is a single object per record. The name of the keeper's baseline-capture phase is never given ('snapshot-db'? 'baseline'?). Also, 'The keeper only boots, holds and tears down' contradicts 'the keeper captures the baseline'.
implementation_impact: The record schema and e2e_phase_durations aggregation (counting each boot once) cannot be implemented without a guess.
suggestion: Specify the exact shape: e.g. boot_id = composite, boot_phases = iteration phases, plus an optional keeper_boot {boot_id, boot_phases} on the first iteration. Name the baseline phase (e.g. 'baseline') and list it in CAP-6.

location: cell-contract.md > Warm container > Reset per iteration
issue: Several points are unspecified or unverifiable: (a) 'all of var/cache' could mean deleting the directory or only its contents (the directory's ownership and permissions matter for www-data recreating it); (b) reset-opcache depends on pgrep being present in the image (procps is often absent in slim images), and the claim 'verified on the three default tags' cannot be checked from the repo (no record or test of it); (c) mysqldump without --databases has no CREATE DATABASE, so the DB name and charset for the recreate must come from parameters.php; (d) snapshot_db/restore_db and DB_PRELUDE live in ps-scenario-run.py, and 'reuse' does not say whether to import that module or move the helpers into a shared place.
implementation_impact: Reset may fail on some tags, turning warm mode off (warm-reset), or may leave var/cache unwritable. A wrong guess silently disables CAP-5.
suggestion: Say 'delete contents of var/cache, keep the directory', specify a pgrep-free detection (e.g. scan /proc/*/comm), point to evidence of the three-tag verification or turn it into a live test, and say where the shared DB helpers live.

location: SPEC.md > CAP-1 success ('With a module that has a blocking E2E bug, no non-canary cell boots until the canary passes'; test exception 'during a loop-back')
issue: Focus cell derivation takes failing cells from any earlier records, including a previous session's, so a new session whose newest failing cell is 8.1:firefox starts with that non-canary cell before the canary has passed. The plan cannot tell 'loop-back' from 'resumed with an old failure', so the test exception ('the focus cell and its version during a loop-back') cannot be expressed in plan terms. It is also unclear whether 'lists' refers to e2e_next_cells or also to e2e_required_cells (blocked-by-scope lists required cells).
implementation_impact: The CAP-1 property test cannot be written unambiguously, and the success claim is false for resumed sessions.
suggestion: Rephrase the test: 'e2e_next_cells contains a non-canary cell only when e2e_step is focus or cold-version and that cell is, or shares the version of, e2e_focus_cell'. Drop the 'during a loop-back' wording, and qualify the CAP-1 success sentence accordingly.

location: SPEC.md > Why ('must cut the wait') / Success signal / Open Questions (wall-clock budget)
issue: The source's load-bearing claim is that E2E 'takes all day', and the goal is to reduce that. No done-criterion measures wall-clock reduction. The success signal checks only structural properties (boot counts, absent phases), and the target budget is left as an open question. Whether the work achieved its purpose cannot be tested.
implementation_impact: There is no acceptance test for the primary goal, and no baseline-versus-after comparison is required.
suggestion: Add a criterion, e.g. 'on bankwire, a clean-module full validation using CAP-6 timings completes in <= X h versus the recorded ~18 h baseline', or at minimum require that a before/after CAP-6 report be produced, with the numeric budget left open.

location: SPEC.md > frontmatter 'sources: []' and Assumptions ('Budi named 9 + Chrome')
issue: The source request (Budi's in-chat request and his answers) is not recorded, even though the banner says source documents are listed for traceability. Two source terms change meaning without being flagged as decisions: 'Chrome' becomes Playwright 'chromium' (not the Chrome channel), and 'version 9' becomes 'newest target', which moves to 10.x if targets change.
implementation_impact: Low: traceability is lost, and the canary default may drift from what Budi asked for.
suggestion: Record the chat request in sources (or quote it). State that 'Chrome' means Playwright chromium and that the canary follows the newest target rather than being pinned to 9.x.

location: cell-contract.md > Runner (ps-run-layer --layer e2e) / Entry points
issue: Several CLI cases are undefined: (a) --layer e2e with neither --cells nor --versions (error, or all configured cells?); (b) a missing --tier (required? the record field tier would be null); (c) --warm or --scenarios-from-failed combined with more than one cell; (d) --cells naming a cell outside the configured set (exit 2 is only implied for the canary).
implementation_impact: Argument validation and the corresponding tests would be guessed.
suggestion: List them explicitly: e.g. require --cells or --versions (exit 2 otherwise), require --tier for e2e, allow --warm/--scenarios-from-failed only with exactly one cell, and exit 2 for unconfigured cells.

location: cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Storage ('ps-run-layer prints e2e_status: skipped') + Runner exit codes
issue: The output channel and format of 'e2e_status: skipped' are not given (stdout line? JSON? stderr?), although the orchestrator must detect it to end the E2E loop. The exit mapping (3/1/0 over appended records) also does not cover a run stopped via --stop-job (today 143) or a child exit 2 combined with other children's records.
implementation_impact: The orchestrator's detection of skipped and stopped would be ad hoc.
suggestion: Specify a machine-readable stdout summary for ps-run-layer --layer e2e (e.g. JSON {e2e_status, appended: [cells], exit}) and add 143/stopped to the exit table.

location: cell-contract.md > Config keys ('--config joins RESERVED_PASSTHROUGH') / Runner (new child flags)
issue: Only --config is added to RESERVED_PASSTHROUGH, but ps-run-layer now owns several child flags: --engines, --run-id, --progress-append, --sequential-browsers, --scenarios, --use-warm, --keep-warm, --warm-owner, --engine-worker. A passthrough copy of any of them would conflict with the value ps-run-layer sets (the same reasoning RESERVED_PASSTHROUGH already applies to --versions and -o). The contract does mention that a --browsers in the passthrough is exit 2.
implementation_impact: The passthrough could override what ps-run-layer guarantees, e.g. engines or run-id, and break slot claims.
suggestion: Add all flags that ps-run-layer sets on children to RESERVED_PASSTHROUGH (including prefix-abbreviation handling) and test it.

location: cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Fields (session: 'passed as --session to every plan call ... both reject a missing ... token (exit 2)') / Docs to update
issue: Making --session mandatory on every ps-plan-layers.py call breaks all current plan invocations, including Phase 1 loops for Layers 1/2/5, run-phases.md commands and the existing tests. The Docs list does not include run-phases' plan commands gaining --session, nor references/adversarial-lens.md, which still says Layer 3 is spawned 'once per run'. The loop-back re-spawn changes that.
implementation_impact: Scope creep and doc drift that the implementer would have to discover.
suggestion: Either require --session only when E2E tier fields are requested, or list every doc and test that must add it. Add adversarial-lens.md (re-spawn on loop-back) to Docs to update.

location: cell-contract.md > Warm container > Owner ('It logs to its own <module>-e2e-<ver>-warm.progress.log') vs SKILL.md / run-phases.md monitoring rule
issue: An idle keeper writes nothing for up to psm_e2e_warm_ttl (60 min). The monitoring rule treats '±3 min without new lines and no DONE' as suspected stuck and offers to stop the job. No heartbeat for the keeper is specified.
implementation_impact: The orchestrator would flag healthy keepers as stuck and propose stopping them.
suggestion: Have the keeper emit ALIVE idle heartbeats (e.g. phase 'idle' every 15 s with remaining TTL), or exempt -warm.progress.log from the stall rule in run-phases.md.

location: cell-contract.md > Config keys > psm_e2e_slots ('Before entering wait-slots, ps-run-layer runs the --cleanup-orphans routine once') vs references/headless.md ('Job yang bukan dimulai run ini tak pernah disentuh')
issue: The automatic cleanup removes dead-owner artifacts of other runs and sessions, including during headless runs, while headless.md forbids touching jobs the run did not start. The contract does not reconcile the two rules.
implementation_impact: Policy ambiguity: should cleanup run automatically in headless mode?
suggestion: State that dead-owner removal through cleanup_decision is allowed in all modes (and update headless.md), or limit the automatic cleanup to interactive runs.

location: cell-contract.md > Plan (e2e_blocked_causes: '{"<ver>:<browser>": cause} for a blocked-* step')
issue: blocked-by-scope is a blocked-* step, but its 'cause' value is never defined (blocked-not-gradeable and blocked-infra have one).
implementation_impact: The output schema would be guessed.
suggestion: Define it, e.g. cause 'out-of-scope' for each cell in e2e_required_cells that the filter removed.

location: cell-contract.md > Aggregate ('e2e_screenshot_dir = common parent of the selected records' screenshots')
issue: Today e2e_screenshot_dir is a list of run folders (ps-aggregate.py normalises it to a list). The contract turns it into a single 'common parent' without saying so, which can collapse to the reports dir or to '/'. SKILL.md's 'Sebut folder screenshot' reads the field, and run-phases' visual review needs the per-run folders.
implementation_impact: A silent type change, plus the risk of a useless root path.
suggestion: Keep it a list (the distinct run folders of the selected records), or state the type change and a fallback when no common parent exists below psm_reports_dir.

location: cell-contract.md > preamble ('They run on a temp copy of bankwire')
issue: The fixture's source path is not given. bankwire exists at modules/bankwire (with tests/e2e) and at /home/budi/dev/prestashop/bankwire (without tests/e2e). The temp copy is also not a git repo, so deleted_specs and scenario-note behaviour differ from a real checkout.
implementation_impact: Minor: the live-test fixture setup has to be guessed.
suggestion: Name the fixture path (modules/bankwire relative to the project root) and say whether the temp copy is git-initialised.
